name: PhotonCamera
hook: Computational photography engine that stacks bursts of underexposed RAW frames into high-dynamic-range photos.
bullets: HDRX merges a burst of RAW frames for real dynamic range
Aligns frames to correct hand shake before merging
Manual focus, shutter, and ISO controls on the viewfinder
Runs on Camera2 with CPU/GPU processing per shot
benefits: Google-Camera-grade HDR without the closed-source app
Huge dynamic range with no plastic over-processed look
Works across multiple lenses, including macro and IR
Keeps shadows clean by averaging out sensor noise
setupSteps: Install PhotonCamera on a Camera2-capable Android phone
Pick a mode and tap the shutter
Wait for the stack to process after each shot
Tune HDRX strength, sharpness, and shadows in settings
details: Most stock camera apps lean on heavy sharpening, aggressive noise reduction, and boosted colors to make images pop. PhotonCamera tries to replicate the magic of Google Camera entirely through open-source algorithms. Instead of one exposure, it captures a rapid burst of underexposed RAW frames, aligns them to correct hand shake, and merges them with custom HDRX algorithms — averaging noise out of the shadows while preserving highlights, for a big jump in dynamic range with none of the plastic look. It drives the Camera2 API and leans on the phone's CPU and GPU for the post-capture stack, so there is a noticeable processing delay after the shutter. That makes it excellent for landscapes, architecture, and static portraits, and a poor choice for fast action.
